findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics if the file is missing, empty, or unreadable
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a domain error type; use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(...) and propagate

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric field values
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (non-numeric second field) causes panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .map_err() on .parse() to return a domain ParseError; do not unwrap

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses index 1 without bounds check after split + collect
findings.failure_mode: a CSV line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to split into at-most-two parts, then .get(1) or match on the tuple; handle missing second field with a typed error

findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 in [65536, u32::MAX] silently truncates to a wrong u16, corrupting data without any error
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value) after parsing to detect overflow and return a typed error

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> via collect for a two-field record
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; also defeats the split_once rule which is designed for single-delimiter extraction
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').map_err(|_| MissingDelimiter)? to get (&str, &str) without allocation, then trim and parse each side

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect inside the parsing/collection pipeline
findings.failure_mode: logging/IO in the core data-processing function makes it non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and mixes shell concerns into the core
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core pipeline; move all I/O/logging to the imperative shell layer outside this function

findings.problem: load_audits performs synchronous fs::read_to_string blocking the caller with no Result wrapper
findings.failure_mode: blocks the calling thread on disk I/O with no error handling; async callers are poisoned
findings.fix: Return impl IntoIterator or Vec<Record> from a pure core function; wrap the fs call in the shell layer with proper error propagation

findings.problem: part.trim().to_string() result is used but the intermediate String allocation is wasteful; trimmed &str is parsed directly on line 19 but the collect on line 15 already owned copies
findings.failure_mode: double-allocation per field: one from to_string() in collect, then another from .clone() on line 18
findings.fix: Avoid collect entirely; use split_once, then .trim() on &str slices directly and parse from &str without intermediate String allocations

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_audits throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis of the parsing pipeline
no allocation tracking (e.g., mimalloc/jemalloc profiling) for per-record Vec<String> allocations
no second-ring evidence (assembly inspection) for bounds-check elimination on parts[1] access
no command-layer documentation for expected CSV format, delimiter count, or field validation contract
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate contains 6 distinct BLOCKER-class violations across unwrap usage, unchecked indexing, lossy as-conversions, split abuse, hidden I/O in the core, and allocation waste. All unwrap/panic/unchecked patterns must be repaired with typed error returns, split_once, get/match access, and try_from before the crate can be considered Holzman-compliant. No benchmark or profiler evidence exists to validate any performance claims.
